chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ayub ibn Nuh from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Bashir ibn Salamah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The best loan is that which brings benefit.'
ai.seo_question: What makes a loan the best according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) defines the superior quality of a loan (*qard*) as one that generates benefit, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for interest-free loans that serve as a means of social welfare rather than mere capital accumulation. This principle underscores the ethical dimension of debt in Islamic finance, where the transaction is viewed as an act of charity or mutual aid, aligning with the broader Shia emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence) in financial dealings.
